title: Kojima et al. 2024 (Dataset A) — An auditory brain-computer interface based on selective attention to multiple tone streams
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 11 healthy participants performing an auditory brain-computer interface task based on selective attention to three tone streams. Participants attended to one of three auditory streams while counting target stimuli, with P300 event-related potentials recorded from 64 EEG channels at 1000 Hz. Classification using Riemannian geometry methods achieved >80% accuracy for 5 subjects and >75% for 9 subjects, demonstrating the feasibility of multi-class auditory BCIs without visual feedback.
methods_description: EEG and EOG signals were recorded at 1000 Hz from 64 EEG channels and 2 EOG channels using Brain Amp DC and MR plus amplifiers (Brain Products GmbH) with a standard 10-20 montage. Musical piano tones were presented to the right ear via headphones using a digital signal processor (Tucker-Davis Technologies System3). Three auditory streams were created using stream segregation with 150 ms tone duration and 180 ms stimulus onset asynchrony. Data preprocessing included bandpass filtering (0.1-100 Hz online; 1-40 Hz for classification), baseline correction, artifact rejection (±100μV EEG, ±500μV EOG), and xDAWN spatial filtering. Classification employed Riemannian geometry covariance matrices and logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation.
